news.title: From Haryana to World Cup dream: Ravi Punia’s mission to transform girls’ lives through football
news.lede: CHENNAI In Haryana’s Alakhpura village, the day begins long before sunrise. Young girls wake up, finish household chores, head to agricultural fields and only if time and their families permit, they lace up their boots For most among them, the dream dies quietly. For a few, it leads to a football pitch, and eventually a life they had barely imagined. Pooja is one of them, who represents India’s under-20 team.

news.title: US judge rejects FIFA bid to intervene in UEFA probe
news.lede: CHENNAI A US judge on Thursday denied an attempt by ​FIFA’s American subsidiaries to intervene in UEFA’s ‌effort to obtain evidence for ​a potential Swiss criminal case ⁠against FIFA President Gianni Infantino over his abandoned World Cup commercial-rights plan. “US FIFA ‌parties have no direct, substantial and legally protectable interest in ‌the subject matter of this ‌application,” ⁠US District Judge Jeannette Vargas ⁠said in her ruling. “In light of this determination, the Court exercises its discretion to decline ​leave to ‌intervene.” European football’s governing body had asked for permission to obtain testimony and documents from FIFA entities in Florida ‌for use in a planned ​criminal complaint in Switzerland against Infantino and other FIFA officials ⁠over a since-abandoned $20 billion World Cup sell-off plan known as FIFA Forward ‌Enterprise (FFE).

news.title: Argentina Extend Head Coach Lionel Scaloni’s Contract Through 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni renewed his contract with the national team on Thursday through 2030, putting him on track to become the first manager to lead La Albiceleste at three World Cups. The 48-year-old Scaloni coached Argentina to the World Cup title in 2022 and a runner-up finish this year after losing the final to Spain. His previous contract was set to expire in December. "After giving it some thought and discussing it with my coaching staff and those close to me, we decided that continuing is the best path forward," Scaloni said at a news conference on Thursday.
